wu: Earth Day Quiz: Teacher shows 5 flashcards (recycle bin, tree, plastic bottle, light bulb, water tap) and asks 'What is this?' Students shout answers in pairs, then teacher adds 'Why is it important?' for quick discussion.
wuAlt: Green Pictionary: Students draw Earth Day words (e.g., 'plant a tree') for teammates to guess.
Quick Poll: 'How many times did you recycle this week?' Students raise hands, count together.
pres: Teacher introduces 'must/should' using flashcards of bad habits (littering, wasting water) and good ones (recycling, turning off lights). Models 'You must not litter' and 'You should recycle'. Checks understanding with thumbs up/down for sentences.
presAlt: Rule Posters: Show examples of eco-rules with must/should, students repeat chorally.
Charades: Teacher acts out eco-actions (e.g., 'turn off lights'), students guess and form sentences.
prac: Error Auction: Teams bid on sentences with mistakes (e.g., 'You must litter'). Winners correct them. Teacher monitors and praises accurate corrections.
pracAlt: Green Dominoes: Match halves of must/should sentences (e.g., 'You should...' + 'save water').
Sentence Relay: Teams race to write correct must/should rules on the board.
ls: Listening Station: Students listen to 3 short dialogues about Earth Day (e.g., 'Should I use a plastic bag? No, you must bring a reusable one'). They tick the rules heard on their passport.
re: Eco-Action Relay: Students line up and race to mime eco-actions (e.g., 'turn off lights', 'put paper in bin') while teammates shout the must/should rule.
prod: Eco-Poster Campaign: Groups design a poster for the American Space with 5 must/should rules (e.g., 'We should use recycled paper'). They present it to the class.
rw: Reading & Writing: Students read a short text about Earth Day at the American Space, then write 3 sentences about what they must/should do there using the text as support.
st: Song: Play 'Reduce, Reuse, Recycle' with actions. Close with 'Today we reviewed must/should for Earth Day. Thank you, class!'
g: Teams answer KET-style questions about must/should rules (e.g., 'What must you do in the library?' 'Be quiet').
Students complete station tasks to collect stamps in their passport, first team to finish wins.
Students act out eco-actions, teammates guess and say the must/should rule.
Teams bid on correct/incorrect must/should sentences, highest bidder wins points for accuracy.
Teams race to write must/should rules on the board, fastest and most accurate wins.
diff: Fast finishers: Design a second eco-poster for their school.
Support learners: Use sentence starters (e.g., 'We should...') for their poster rules.
hw: Complete the pre-assessment checklist for the year.
Design a 5-rule green poster for your home with must/should.
Write 3 sentences about what you must/should do to help the planet.
tip: Use local examples (e.g., 'We should save water in Oujda') to make the rules culturally relevant and increase engagement.
